clue.text: Where you might see koala in difficulties

definitions.meaning: a koala lives high in a eucalyptus, the Australian gum tree
an idiom for being stuck in an awkward fix with no easy way down

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a koala's literal perch in a eucalyptus, and the idiom for being stranded in trouble.

clue.text: Employed and unemployed seem equally depressed at first sight

indicators.note: at first sight asks for the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A gloomy observation that workers and jobless people look just as miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employed' and 'unemployed' look like a pair of opposites in the definition; only the first is, and 'unemployed' gives its U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something employed has been put to work or made use of, a simple synonym.

clue.text: A record's range

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A remark on how wide a span a single record covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' reads as musical compass, but it is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps form a European mountain range.

clue.text: Where light may be located, in secret

definitions.meaning: a ceiling light hangs below the ceiling rose, the plaster or plastic fitting holding its flex
the phrase translates the Latin sub rosa, meaning confidentially

explanation.definitionFit: A ceiling rose holds a hanging light; the idiom from Latin sub rosa means confidentially.

clue.text: Bore taking drink with leading journalist

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
ED is short for editor, the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: Someone tedious who has a drink with the newspaper's top writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person, but it is the past tense of bear, meaning carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Toted means carried, the same past-tense sense as bore from bear.

clue.text: English intimate support for community and its environment

parts.note: cosy means snug and intimate
a stem supports a flower or leaf

explanation.surface: Snug English backing for a local community and its surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecology's term for a group of living things together with their physical surroundings.

clue.text: Line unnecessary at the end to lower boat

indicators.note: the line is not needed at the tail, so that letter is dropped from the end

parts.note: to lour or lower is to frown or scowl

explanation.surface: Advice that a rope is not needed at the stern to let a boat down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' suggests lowering a boat, but it rhymes with 'flower' and means to frown.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed barge, a kind of boat.

clue.text: Give way about revision of rating scale

indicators.note: about means the yielding word goes round the reworked letters

parts.note: to cede is to yield or give way

indicators.note: a revision rewrites the word rating, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to back down over a rewritten rating system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give way' reads as a road instruction, and 'revision of' signals rearranging rating, which 'about' places inside the yielding word.
explanation.definitionFit: Centigrade is the temperature scale now usually called Celsius.

clue.text: Troubled lad we care about, tired of life

indicators.note: about means the word for anxiety surrounds the shuffled letters

parts.note: care in the sense of anxiety is worry

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed, so lad we are rearranged

explanation.surface: A distressed young man and friends are anxious about someone fed up with living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled' looks like describing the lad, but it signals the anagram of lad we; 'about' then wraps the word for care round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: World-weary describes someone jaded and bored with existence.

clue.text: Voyagers make haste

definitions.meaning: a party of explorers travelling together is called this
an old sense means promptness or speed

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a travelling party of explorers, and also speed, as in 'with all expedition'.

clue.text: Standing back to make knot

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for standing in the reverse direction

parts.note: standing means status or rank

explanation.surface: Someone stepping backwards to tie a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A knar is a knot or gnarl in a tree trunk.

clue.text: Check noise of birds from Norway, perhaps

parts.note: to scan is to check or examine
a din is a loud noise
avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: An instruction to check the racket of birds from Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Norway as one example of the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is one of the Scandinavian countries, so a Norwegian is an example.

clue.text: Issue raised by right-hand man who's loving and giving?

definitions.meaning: Man Friday is Crusoe's faithful servant, so his issue is his offspring
the nursery rhyme 'Monday's child' says the child of this weekday is loving and giving

explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is a Man Friday, so his offspring; the rhyme calls that weekday's baby loving and giving.

clue.text: Saw report on heroin, and article, accepted by yearly meeting

indicators.note: accepted by means the meeting takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: AGM is an annual general meeting
a pop is a sharp bang or report
H is slang for heroin
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A story about drugs and a newspaper piece being heard at the annual meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb, but it is a noun meaning a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: An apophthegm is a pithy maxim, as is an old saw.

clue.text: In a manner of speaking, assimilating a clue

indicators.note: assimilating means absorbing, so the second a is taken inside

parts.note: diction is one's way of pronouncing and choosing words

explanation.surface: A remark that, so to speak, someone is taking in a crossword hint.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole opening reads as the stock phrase 'in a manner of speaking', hiding a split after the first word; 'assimilating' takes the second a inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a hint or sign, and an indication is the same.

clue.text: Broad-minded worshipper, possibly, in the past

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of in the past could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone who perhaps was a tolerant believer in earlier times.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheist sees God in everything, a very inclusive view of worship.

clue.text: Cross one river both ways on board

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first pieces sit above the next

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one and R stands for river

indicators.note: both ways says one river is read forwards and then backwards

parts.note: the same I and R, used a second time
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Ford a river in both directions while aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb to go over the river, but it is an adjective meaning irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross means angry or tetchy, as does irritable.

clue.text: Bottle opener — vessel requires it

annotationWithheld.why: Bottle opener - vessel requires it (5): BOTTLE gives NERVE as definition, but no parse found for 'opener - vessel requires it' giving the letters

clue.text: Superior poet

definitions.meaning: the head of a priory is a religious superior; also means earlier
Matthew ... was an English poet of the early 18th century

explanation.definitionFit: A prior heads a religious house, and Matthew Prior was an English poet.

clue.text: Follow-up to bill without a balance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the reminder goes round the a

parts.note: a reminder is the letter sent after an unpaid bill

explanation.surface: A second demand comes after an invoice when there is no money in the account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The balance is what is left over, the rest.

clue.text: Passing an oral — it isn't complicated

indicators.note: complicated letters are tangled, so an oral it isn't are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting through a spoken exam that is actually straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' suggests passing the exam, but it means fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Transitional means temporary, in passing from one state to another.

clue.text: Haven provided by American organisation on island

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the organisation sits above the island

parts.note: OAS is the Organization of American States

explanation.surface: A refuge set up by a US body on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a refuge or place of peace, as a haven is.

clue.text: In speech, depict member

indicators.note: in speech means the word for depict is spoken, giving the same sound

parts.note: to limn is to depict or portray

explanation.surface: Someone describing a club member in a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests a club, but is an arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the body is a limb.

clue.text: Bet poet's lost some money in the past

indicators.note: lost means the poet has had the coin taken away

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
D was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A poet who gambled and lost cash long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has'. D, from Latin denarius, marked the old British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put into a poker pot before dealing.

clue.text: A lot of water gets state backing

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the state's name is read from the end

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name of the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: A large amount of water receives official support.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes, a large body of water.

clue.text: African hell home to a Scot

parts.note: the abyss is the bottomless pit of hell
in means at home
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a stock Scottish name

explanation.surface: Scottish lodger in an African inferno.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the old name for Ethiopia, so an Abyssinian is an African from there.

clue.text: Suitable presents, you might say, for this flirtatious female

indicators.note: you might say means the furs are spoken, giving the same sound

parts.note: mink coats are the sort of lavish gift for such a woman

explanation.surface: A suitor wonders what gifts would be fitting for a coquettish woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is a cheeky, flirty young woman.

clue.text: Being smart and good-looking

parts.note: a being is a person
able means clever or smart

explanation.surface: Being clever and attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like it goes with good-looking, but means clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Personable means pleasant in appearance and manner, attractive.
